items.title: Black Forest Labs launches Flux 3 Image with multi-step editing that leaves the rest of your picture alone
items.excerpt: Black Forest Labs has released Flux 3 Image, the image side of its Flux 3 model family. It supports multi-step edits without changing other parts of the image, lets users compose scenes with bounding boxes and up to ten reference images, and outputs up to 4K. Open weights are coming in the next few weeks.
items.rationale: Major image-model release: localized multi-step edits, bounding-box composition with 10 references, 4K output, open weights coming -- directly changes how designers iterate on visuals.

items.title: ClassCAD.ai brings its CAD model-building MCP to your system
items.excerpt: ClassCAD.ai has been launched as an AI-driven embeddable CAD, that's a self contained MCP able to build CAD in your Claude/Codex
items.rationale: New product launch: a self-contained CAD MCP that lets Claude/Codex build real CAD models -- a different company and product from the OwlCAD browser launch published 10-01.

items.title: From Reusable to Regeneratable: Rethinking the Shared UI Component Library
items.excerpt: Regeneration has changed reuse economics. A model pointed at a solid design system can produce most standard UI on demand, so paying to keep a canonical component package alive is much harder to justify than it used to be. Keep the design system, tokens, guidelines and tests central. They are what actually buy you consistency.
items.rationale: Fresh, substantive argument for design-system teams: keep tokens, guidelines and tests central and let models regenerate components -- reframes what a DS team maintains.

items.title: Stop blaming the model for slow AI. Using Doherty's threshold as a guideline.
items.excerpt: Doherty's threshold has moved from the answer to the acknowledgment: designing AI products for perceived speed is a week of front-end work and a definition of done, not cheaper inference.
items.rationale: Highly actionable UX guidance: design AI products for perceived speed via instant acknowledgment, a front-end fix designers can ship tomorrow.

items.title: Ideogram says its new model can edit part of an image without messing up the rest
items.excerpt: Ideogram's new model Ideogram 4.5 promises to edit only the areas you want while keeping the rest of the image intact. It ships with native 2K resolution starting at 0.8 cents per image, and partners like Runway, Pika, and Leonardo AI are already on board. An open-weight release is planned.
items.rationale: Separate model release from a different company (Ideogram 4.5): region-only edits, native 2K at 0.8 cents/image, already available through Runway, Pika and Leonardo.
